newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood actress Joanne Dru dies at 73.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood actress Joanne Dru dies at 73.

text.p: Joanne Dru, an actress who starred in films during the 1940s and '50s, died Tuesday at her home in Beverly Hills of respiratory failure following a lengthy illness, it was announced Thursday. She was 73.

Dru was born in Logan, West Virginia, in 1923. In 1940 Dru moved to New York, where she worked as a model. Her break came when Al Jolson cast her, along with Joyce Mathews and Jinx Falkenberg, as one of the beautiful showgirls in his last Broadway show, "Hold Onto Your Hats", which co-starred Martha Raye.
Dru's first screen appearance was in 1946, when she was cast opposite Bing Crosby in the film "Abie's Irish Rose."

Dru appeared in numerous films throughout the 1940s and 1950s but is perhaps best remembered for her roles in Western classics such as Howard Hawks' "Red River" and John Ford's "She Wore a Yellow Ribbon."
Additional screen credits included "All the King's Men", "The Pride of St. Louis", "Mr. Belvedere Rings the Bell", "Durango" and "The Wild and Innocent."
In the early 1960s, Dru starred in the TV series "Guestward Ho" for two years and guested on dozens of other TV shows.
